statement: Starting tomorrow, Lena will go to the library every $4$th day, the pool every $6$th day and the park every $10$th day. So she goes to the library on days $4, 8, 12, \ldots$, the pool on days $6, 12, 18, \ldots$ and the park on days $10, 20, 30, \ldots$. During days $1$ through $365$, on how many days does she go to both the library and the pool but not the park?

choices.misconception: I counted the days she goes to all three places, the multiples of $60$, instead of the days she skips the park.
I thought the library and the pool line up every $4 \cdot 6 = 24$ days, so I counted $365 \div 24$ rounded down, and I also forgot to remove the park days.
I subtracted the $6$ days with all three places twice, $30 - 6 - 6 = 18$, instead of once.
I counted the days that are multiples of $12$ but forgot to remove the days she also goes to the park.

hints: On which days does she go to both the library and the pool?
The library and pool days are the multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(4, 6) = 12$. Among them, the park days are the multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(12, 10) = 60$.
There are $\lfloor 365 / 12 \rfloor = 30$ multiples of $12$ and $\lfloor 365 / 60 \rfloor = 6$ multiples of $60$ in the range.

solutions.reliable: A day is a library and pool day exactly when it is a multiple of both $4$ and $6$, that is, a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(4, 6) = 12$. From $1$ to $365$ there are $30$ such days, since $12 \cdot 30 = 360$. Of these, the park days are the multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(12, 10) = 60$, and there are $6$ of them ($60, 120, \ldots, 360$). So the answer is $30 - 6 = 24$.
